cases.expected: ESP32-S3 only and IDF >= 5.5 enforced at configure/compile time

cases.title: A07: C receiver validates only part of the mandatory envelope (static reproduction)
cases.input: compare schema 'required' with the fields handle_line() inspects
cases.expected: all 8 mandatory fields validated before acting (as the Python decoder does)
cases.actual: validated: ['protocol_version', 'type']; NOT validated: ['device_id', 'session_id', 'sequence_number', 'timestamp_ms', 'source', 'payload']. A HELLO such as {"protocol_version":1,"type":"HELLO"} reaches dc_announce() in C but is rejected by the Python parser (QA-IOT-002)
cases.notes: Defect A07 is still open; reproduction is by source inspection only, not execution.

cases.title: Real CAN is disabled and guarded; Wi-Fi/MicroSD/ADC/RTC are not implemented
cases.expected: CAN guard present; no TWAI/Wi-Fi/SD/ADC/RTC usage
cases.actual: {"real_can_flag_zero": true, "compile_error_if_enabled": true, "twai_used": false, "wifi_used": false, "sd_used": false, "adc_used": false, "rtc_used": false}
cases.notes: Static. Those features are Not Implemented in M1, hence also not tested.

cases.title: Line-size limit is consistent between C (4096) and Python (4096 incl. LF); oversize is discarded with an ERROR
cases.expected: same limit; overflow discards until LF and sends OVERSIZED_MESSAGE
cases.actual: {"DC_MAX_LINE": ["main/device_protocol.h:7: #define DC_MAX_LINE 4096"], "input_buffer": ["main/device_protocol.c:11: static char input[DC_MAX_LINE];"], "overflow_guard": ["main/device_protocol.c:133: if (input_length >= sizeof(input) - 1) { discarding = true; input_length = 0; }"], "python_MAX_LINE_BYTES": 4096, "usb_rx_tx": ["main/main.c:30: .tx_buffer_size = 8192, .rx_buffer_size = 4096"]}

cases.title: Test mode: data labelled DEVICE_TEST, event upload not advertised
Error behaviour in the C receiver
cases.expected: INVALID_MESSAGE / UNSUPPORTED_MESSAGE / OVERSIZED_MESSAGE exist; no vehicle-changing command
cases.actual: main/device_protocol.c:113: send_error("INVALID_MESSAGE", ms);; main/device_protocol.c:117: send_error("UNSUPPORTED_MESSAGE", ms);; main/device_protocol.c:128: if (discarding) send_error("OVERSIZED_MESSAGE", timestamp_ms);
cases.notes: No command handler writes to hardware: only HELLO (re-announce) and ACK (ignored) are accepted.
